PART 3
[8 marks]
Questions 19 to 26
You are going to read an extract about the Malaysian night market. For questions 19 to 26, choose
the correct answer ( A, B, C or D ).
Pasar malam is a Malay word that literally means 'night market', Pasar malam is a street market
set up in the evening, usually in residential neighbourhoods. It brings together a collection of stalls that
usually sell goods such as fruits, vegetables, food, toys, clothes, shoes, alarm clocks and ornaments at
cheap or at least, reasonable prices. You can get almost anything at these night markets.
Pasar malam traders rotate around different neighbourhoods on different days of the week. Prices
are not fixed and as such haggling over prices is a common practice at such markets. The market starts
off slowly and as early as three in the afternoon. Traders often try to nab the favoured spot, set up stalls
and put their goods on display. Within a short time, the pace increases and the space that used to be a
formal, quiet car park or residential area is now a bustling marketplace with varying smells, colours,
noise and people.
The whole area is transformed and you can see people young and old alike weaving in and out
of the stalls, occasionally stopping to look at the items on display and to find out the price of an item.
Smells adrift all around the market, the smell of nasi lemak, fried chicken, fried noodles and other types
of food, and many people cannot resist the temptation to buy something for their dinner. The place is
rackety, with people calling and laughing, machines humming and pumping, all with a purpose.
As you squeeze through the crowd, the first thing that catches your attention is the many fruit and
vegetable stalls. The colourful fruits and the lush and plentiful vegetables are all arranged beautifully
and customers are spoilt for choice. You have an array of local and imported fruits to choose from.
Even the prices are displayed and all you have to do is pick out the fruits you want and pay without
even saying a word. If you are not pleased with the price quoted, you can always move to the next
stall. If you are not into vegetables and fruits, then head to the fish and meat stalls. Here, you can buy a
whole chicken or cut pieces to suit your taste. The meat is fresh and succulent and looks full of flavour.
A variety of fresh fish can be bought here and the trader will even take the trouble to clean it for you
for free.
Walk further on and you will see the clothes stalls. The clothes are reasonably priced and of the
latest fashion. It caters to the young and old. Clothing items such as pyjamas, T-shirts, pants, batik
housecoats, dresses, shirts, undergarments and even shoes can be bought here. The prices are not fixed
and if something catches your eye, you can ask for the price and try to get a reduction. Flexibility is the
key here. There is no hard and fast rule for prices.
Finally, a visit to the night market will not be complete if you do not head to the various food stalls.
You have Western and local cakes, banana fritters, laksa, fried noodles and numerous other kinds of
food to suit your taste buds. Most of the food on sale is freshly cooked. After you have placed your
order, you need to wait a few minutes to get your order No service charges at all. A simple meal at a
reasonable and affordable price! What more can we ask for? You get your money's worth here and there
is no room for complaints and dissatisfaction.
It takes only thirty to forty minutes to walk around the whole market. It is time well spent. Not only
do you get to buy things cheaply but you can also enjoy the environment and take note of the myriad of
people who throng the night markets. The night markets in Malaysia are a big draw, bringing together
both tourists and locals. It is, after all, a great place to just walk about and savour the aromas of local
street delicacies and buy items at reasonable prices.

PART 4
[6 marks]
You are going to read an article about a popular online game. Six sentences have been
removed from the article. Choose from the sentences A to H the one which fits each gap (27
to 32). There are two extra sentences which you do not need to use.
Player Unknown's Battlegrounds (PUBG)
Player Unknown's Battlegrounds (PUBG) is an online multiplayer battle royale game
developed and published by PUBG Corporation, a subsidiary of South Korean video game
company, Bluchole, 27. In the game, up to one hundred players parachute onto an
island and scavenge for weapons and equipment to kill others while avoiding getting killed
themselves. Players can choose to enter the match solo, as a duo, or with a small team of up
to four people.
The plane's flight path across the map varies with each round, requiring players to
quickly determine the best time to eject and parachute to the ground, 28. These items
are procedurally distributed throughout the map at the start of a match, with certain high-risk
zones typically having better equipment.
29. This means that surviving players are directed to tighter areas to force
encounters. During the course of the match, random regions of the map are highlighted in red
and bombed, posing a threat to players who remain in that area. At the completion of each
round, players gain in-game currency based on their performance. 30. The last player
or team standing wins the round.
31. The game has sold over 70 million copies on personal computers and game
consoles as of 2020. PUBG has received positive reviews from critics, who found that while
the game had some technical flaws, it presented new types of game play that could be easily
approached by players of any skill level. The game has been attributed to popularising the
battle royale genre, with a number of unofficial Chinese clones also being produced following
its success. 32. PUBG Corporation has run several small tournaments and introduced
in-game tools to broadcast the game to spectators, as they wish for it to become a popular e-
sport. On a side note, the game has also been banned in some countries for allegedly being
harmful and addictive to younger players.
Source: The Internet

PART 5
[8 MARKS]
We interviewed six ardent readers from the Synergy book Club. Read the texts below and answer the
questions that follow.
A-Joyce- ALL AROUND THE TOWN by Mary Clark
I have always preferred detective novels and this author is one of the best in this category. The novel
starts with Laurie Kenyon, a college student, who is accused of murdering her professor. She has no
memory of the crime and seeks help from a psychiatrist. The story revealed by the psychiatrist about
Laurie takes a twisted turn and will hold your attention till the end.
B-Alina- A THOUSAND SPLENDID SUNS by Khaled Hosseini
This award-winning bestseller by Khaled Hosseini really touched my heart. I cried while reading it as
it was just so moving. Set in Kabul, Mariam befriends Laila. Their friendship known no bounds and
overcomes the most daunting obstacles in a beautiful and heroic way.
C- Bob- AND THEN THERE WERE NONE by Agatha Christie
This book, by the world-renowned Queen of Crime, is by far the best mystery I have ever read. I just
had to stay up the whole night till I was done! The story is full of twists, as expected from Christie.
Mysterious invitations, disappearing guests, an island amidst a thunderstorm, murders following a
nursery rhymes all intricately woven to thrill the readers until the end.
D- Su Yin- PERCY JACKSON AND THE LIGHTNING THIEF by RIck Riordan
I wanted to read the book first before watching the movie adaptation. I was mesmerized by the novel
as if offered so much. Adventure, myths, Greek gods, magic, legends and so much more. I was totally
captivated till the end.
E- Amy- WHITE FANG by Jack London
Being neither a dog nor a wolf, White Fang faces trouble finding his place in the world. He learns to
survive and defend himself. I love how White Fang is changed from savage beast to a gentle, wise
animal by the kindness of one man. It really is an inspiring story.
F- Joey- HARRY PORTER AN THE CURSED CHILD by J.K. Rowling
I have enjoyed all the books in the Harry Porter series and this is the last one. I spent two days
reading it till the end. I am so happy to finally get closure about Harry and his family. This book is
magical, just like the others!
